rationale: OOPack v1p8 is a small C++ benchmark dominated by hot numeric loops and object-oriented dispatch (virtual calls, object construction/destruction), with no available static source profile, so the weighting favors low-cost, low-risk passes: SUB and SPLIT get strong weights (cheap arithmetic and block-level transformations that diversify code with negligible runtime or size impact), IBR is kept moderately weighted since basic-block rotation hides control-flow structure with little overhead, and ICALL is moderately weighted to obfuscate the benchmark's call/virtual-dispatch patterns at acceptable indirect-call cost. BCF, FLA, and IGV receive high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights to suppress their application: OOPack's tight inner loops would suffer materially from bogus-control-flow flattening and global-control-flow graph manipulation, while its small overall size means BCF's code-blowup yields poor resistance-per-byte. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low for the well-tested local passes and slightly higher for control-flow-heavy passes (FLA, IGV, BCF) so that, combined with their cost weights, they are effectively discouraged; if the driver requires all passes present, these three will still only fire on functions whose feature vectors strongly favor them.
